## MarcXML Configuration
### 001 (Control Number)
**Explanation:** The unique identifier for this specific record within the system. This is administrative metadata generated by the cataloging system to track the record itself. <br />
**Example:** =001  51498

### 005 (Date and Time of Latest Transaction)
**Explanation:** A system-generated timestamp of when the record was last modified. This is administrative metadata generated by the cataloging system to track the record itself. <br />
**Example:** =005  20260415103355.0 (Format: YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.0).

### 100 (Main Entry - Personal Name)
**Explanation:** Contains the system control number or URI of the established authority record for the person listed in the field. The Excel only had 45128. This record shows the full name ($a), dates ($d), and the ID ($0). <br />
**Example:** =100  1#$a Elgar, Edward $d 1857-1934 $0 45128

### 130 $m (Medium of performance for music)
**Explanation:** Details the specific instruments or voices the piece was written for. <br />
**Comparison:** Like the 100 field, in excel separated the title, medium, and key. Here they are combined, and a unique Authority ID ($0) for this specific piece of music is added. <br />
**Example:** =130 0#  $m V, orch

### 130 $r (Key for music) 
**Explanation:** States the musical key of the work in the uniform title. <br />
**Example:** 130 0# $r e

### 130 $a (Uniform title)
**Explanation:** The core, established title of a work used to bring all its iterations together. <br />
**Example:** 130 0# $a Sea slumber song

### 380 (Form of work)
**Explanation:** The overarching class, genre, or category to which a work belongs. <br />
**Comparison:** The Excel just had the text "Songs". This record has two 380 fields, detailing specific choral forms, and includes the vocabulary authority ID ($0) for those terms. <br />
**Example 1:** 380 ## $a Songs <br />
**Example 2:** =380  ## $a Choral music $0 50001734 <br />
**Example 3:** =380  ## $a Part songs $0 25460 <br />

### 031 (Musical Incipits Information)
**Comparison:** Notice how $a, $b, $c, $d, $o, $r, and $t are all in one continuous string here. It also adds a new subfield $2 pe (indicating the encoding format, likely "Plaine and Easie Code").
   - 031$a <br />
        Proper Name: Musical Incipits Information -> Number of work <br />
        Explanation: The serial number of a work within a larger collection. <br />
        Example: 031 ## $a 1 <br />
   - 031$b <br />
        Proper Name: Musical Incipits Information -> Number of movement <br />
        Explanation: Identifies the specific movement of the musical piece. <br />
        Example: 031 ## $b 2 <br />
   - 031$c <br />
        Proper Name: Musical Incipits Information -> Number of excerpt <br />
        Explanation: Identifies a specific excerpt within a movement. <br />
        Example: 031 ## $c 1 <br />
   - 031$d <br />
        Proper Name: Musical Incipits Information -> Caption or heading <br />
        Explanation: The textual heading or tempo marking for the incipit. <br />
        Example: 031 ## $d Andantino <br />
   - 031$t
        Proper Name: Musical Incipits Information -> Text incipit <br />
        Explanation: The opening lyrics or text of a vocal musical work. <br />
        Example: 031 ## $t Sea-birds are asleep <br />
   - 031$r <br />
        Proper Name: Musical Incipits Information -> Key or mode <br />
        Explanation: The musical key or mode in which the incipit is written. <br />
        Example: 031 ## $r e <br />
   - 031$o <br />
        Proper Name: Musical Incipits Information -> Clef <br />
        Explanation: The clef used in the musical notation of the incipit. <br /> 
        Example: 031 ## $o 4/4 <br /> 
     
**Full Example:** =031  ##$a 1 $b 1 $c 1 $d Larghetto $o 4 /4 $r g $t I met at eve the Prince of Sleep $2 pe

### 690 (Local Subject Access Field)
**Comparison:** Combined on one line. It shows the Christopher Kent Elgar catalog ($a KenE), the specific item number ($n 1925-2), and the local system ID ($0 51004444). <br /> <br /> 
   - 690$0<br /> 
        Proper Name: Local Subject Access Field -> Authority record control number or standard number<br /> 
        Explanation: Connects a locally defined subject heading to a specific vocabulary URI or local authority record.<br /> 
        Example: 690 ## $0 KenE 2013690<br /> 
   - 690$n<br /> 
        Proper Name: Local Subject Access Field -> Number of part/section of a work<br /> 
        Explanation: Designates a part or section number when a local subject refers to a specific portion of a larger work or series.<br /> 
        Example: 690 ## $n 1899-8<br />
     
**Full Example:** =690  #7 $a KenE $n 1925-2 $0 51004444 <br /> 

### 040 (Cataloging Source)
**Explanation:** Shows which organizations originally created and modified the record.<br /> 
**Example:** =040  ##$aDE-633$cDE-633$erismg (Created and transcribed by DE-633, using "rismg" cataloging rules).

### 500 (See Also From Tracing - Personal Name)
**Comparison:** The Excel only had the ID (51041226) and relationship (lyr). This record shows the lyricist's full name, dates, ID, and relationship code all together.<br /> 
**Example:** =500  1#$aDe la Mare, Walter$d1873-1956$051041636$4lyr<br /> 

### 046 (Special Coded Dates)
**Comparison:** Very similar to excel, but presented on one line.<br /> 
**Example:** =046  ##$k1925$zFinished 1925-07-22.
